name: 2025 livery
description: All-white fuselage with a very large teal-green lowercase 'transavia' running from just behind the forward door to past the wing; solid teal-green fin with a big white 't' monogram; all-green engines with a white 't'; white sharklets with a small green 't'.

sources.title: F-HXIF A320neo, Transavia France, Palma (CC BY 4.0)
sources.note: Left side, 2026-09: the 2025 scheme: green fin with white t, the long title, green engines, white sharklet with a green t.

sources.title: Transavia brand refresh write-up (Made Good Designs)
sources.note: Dates: first new-livery A320neo rolled out 2025-09-10, refresh presented 2025-10-22 (Studio Dumbar/DEPT), first Dutch A321neo PH-YHR December 2025; all-green engines; white sharklets with a green T outside, green with a white T inside; a logo on the belly.

logos.description: Transavia's 't': a thick rounded lowercase t, the crossbar long to the front and short behind, the foot hooking forward-up into a curl.
The 't' in white on the outboard side of the green cowling.
A small green 't' high on the white outer face of the sharklet (white on green inside).

titles.style: Huge heavy geometric lowercase, rounded counters, tight spacing; the windows run through it. Ascender (t) height given.

notes: Introduced on new A320neos (Transavia France) and A321neos (Transavia, from PH-YHR); most of the fleet, including all 737-800s and many neos, still wears the 2015 scheme (standard-2015) as of late 2026, and repaints run over several years. The belly logo the brand write-up mentions isn't seen in any photo here; small 'AIR FRANCE KLM GROUP' and 'AIRBUS A320neo' marks aren't drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on F-HXIF and F-HXIB (A320neo, 2026), placed by the doors: 'transavia' runs x 0.20-0.67 (it had stopped about 1 m short); its lowercase 0.7 of the t's height.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation. Replaces the 2015 scheme (white fin with a green disc, colored belly marks) from September 2025.
